explanation: Subject + present-tense verb + indefinite article + noun.
Adjectives agree with the subject's gender: 'stanca' for a woman.
Nationalities are not capitalized in Italian.
'Noi abbiamo' = 'we have'; 'un cane' = 'a dog' (m.).

english: The book is on the table.
explanation: 'Su' contracts with the article: su + il = sul.
'Bere' is irregular: io bevo, tu bevi, lui beve…
'Andare a + place'. With 'scuola' no article is used.
'A casa' is a fixed expression with no article.
'Parlare' (regular -are): parlo, parli, parla, parliamo…
Masculine nouns ending in -o usually take -i in the plural.
'Grande' is invariable in the singular for both genders.
'Un caffè' = a coffee. 'Caffè' is masculine.
Possessives normally take the article: 'il mio amico'.
'Leggere' (irregular -ere): leggo, leggi, legge…
'Dormire' (regular -ire): dormo, dormi, dorme…
'Amico' → plural 'amici' (note the hard 'c' becomes 'ch' in 'amici'? — no: 'amici' is correct, the -ci is soft).
Cities take 'a': abito a Milano, a Roma, a Napoli.
'Buona' agrees with 'pizza' (feminine singular).
'Volere' is irregular: voglio, vuoi, vuole, vogliamo…
Days are not capitalized in Italian.
'Andare' takes 'essere'. Past participle agrees with the subject.
Modal verbs are followed by the infinitive: devo + comprare.
'Potere' (can) + infinitive expresses ability/possibility.

grammar_point: volere + infinitive + definite article with language
explanation: Languages take the article: l'italiano, il francese, lo spagnolo.
Most transitive verbs use 'avere'; participle does not agree by default.
Adverbs of quantity often follow the participle.
'La' = her/it (f.) goes BEFORE the conjugated verb.
'Non … più' = no longer / not anymore.
Reflexive: 'svegliarsi' → mi sveglio, ti svegli, si sveglia…
Reflexives use 'essere' in the past; participle agrees in number/gender.

english: He arrived late because of the train.
italian: È arrivato tardi a causa del treno.
explanation: 'A causa di' = 'because of'; 'di + il' = 'del'.

english: I always drink coffee in the morning.
italian: Bevo sempre il caffè la mattina.
explanation: Parts of the day take the article: la mattina, il pomeriggio.

english: I have already seen this film.
grammar_point: passato prossimo + 'già' between aux. and participle
explanation: Adverbs like 'già', 'ancora', 'mai' go between auxiliary and participle.

english: We go to the sea in summer.
explanation: 'A + il = al'. Seasons use 'in': in estate, in inverno.

english: She speaks well because she studies a lot.
explanation: 'Perché' connects a result with its reason.

english: While I was eating, the phone rang.
italian: Mentre mangiavo, il telefono ha squillato.
grammar_point: imperfetto for ongoing action + passato prossimo for interrupting event
explanation: Imperfetto sets the background; passato prossimo describes the punctual event.

english: I have known him for two years.
explanation: Italian uses the present tense + 'da' where English uses 'for/since' with the perfect.
'Ci sono' = there are. 'Molte persone' is f. plural.
Object pronouns can attach to the end of an infinitive: aiutare + mi → aiutarmi.

english: If I have time, I'll call you.
explanation: Italian commonly uses present + present for likely conditions.

grammar_point: subjunctive after verbs of opinion ('penso che')
explanation: Verbs of opinion typically trigger the subjunctive: 'sia' = subj. of 'essere'.

english: When I was a child, I used to play in the park.
italian: Quando ero bambino, giocavo al parco.
explanation: Imperfetto describes ongoing or habitual situations in the past.

english: Tomorrow I will go to the doctor.
grammar_point: futuro semplice + 'da' for going to a person
explanation: 'Da + person' = at/to that person's place: 'dal medico' = at the doctor's.

english: I would like a glass of water.
explanation: 'Vorrei' is the conditional of 'volere'; the standard polite form.
'Sperare che' triggers the subjunctive; 'stia' is subj. of 'stare'.

english: Although it is raining, I'm going out.
explanation: 'Anche se' = 'even though / although' and uses the indicative.

english: I have been studying Italian for a year.
grammar_point: present + 'da' for duration up to now
explanation: Italian uses present + 'da' where English uses present perfect continuous.

english: If I had time, I would travel more.
italian: Se avessi tempo, viaggerei di più.
explanation: 'Se avessi … viaggerei' = unreal/hypothetical present condition.

english: I don't know whether he is coming.
explanation: 'Se' meaning 'whether/if' in indirect questions takes the indicative here.

english: I had already eaten when he arrived.
italian: Avevo già mangiato quando è arrivato.
grammar_point: trapassato prossimo for an action before another past action
explanation: Trapassato prossimo (avevo + participle) marks anteriority in the past.

english: It's important to study every day.
explanation: 'È + adj. + infinitive' is a common impersonal pattern.

english: I'm going to Italy to learn the language.
italian: Vado in Italia per imparare la lingua.
explanation: 'Per + infinitive' expresses purpose ('in order to').
'Mi chiamo' literally means 'I call myself'.
'Come ti chiami?' uses 'ti' (yourself) for informal 'you'.
Use 'stare' (not essere) when asking about wellbeing.
Reply with 'sto bene' to 'come stai?'.
'Dove' = where; subject pronoun is dropped.
Use 'a' before city names with 'abitare'.
Italian uses 'avere' (to have) for age, not 'essere'.
Literally 'how many years do you have?'
'Dell'' = di + l' (some); used for unspecified quantities.
'Aiutarmi' = aiutare + mi (help me) - object pronoun attaches to infinitive.
'Non' goes before the verb to negate.
Plural 'lingue' (the noun ends in -e in singular feminine).
Use 'a' (without article) for 'a scuola', 'a casa', 'a letto'.
'A casa' = home, no article needed.
'Alle' (a + le) is used for hours from 2 onwards: alle due, alle tre...
'Alzarsi' is reflexive: mi alzo, ti alzi, si alza...

english: There is a cat in the garden.
explanation: 'C'è' for singular 'there is'; 'ci sono' for plural.
'Molte' agrees with feminine plural 'persone'.
'Ogni' (every) is invariable: ogni giorno, ogni anno...
'Mal di...' for body aches: mal di testa, mal di stomaco.
Italian uses 'fare' for weather: fa caldo, fa freddo, fa bel tempo.
'Stare + gerundio' = present continuous, similar to '-ing' in English.
'Piacere' literally 'to be pleasing'; 'pizza' is the subject.
'Piacciono' (plural) because the songs are the subject.
'Ti' (informal you) + piace (singular) + article + noun.
'Non' goes before the indirect pronoun 'mi'.
Italian uses avere (not be) for hunger, thirst, sleep, fear, etc.
Same pattern: avere + sete (thirst).
'Sonno' = sleep (the noun); 'avere sonno' = to be sleepy.
Use avere (not essere) for being cold/hot personally.
'Chiuso' (closed) is the past participle of chiudere, used as an adjective.
'In' before indefinite articles or no article (in città, in casa).
'Caffè' is invariable in plural (no -i).
Singular 'quanto' for one item; 'quanto costano' for plural.
'Euro' is invariable in plural in Italian.
'Cercare' takes a direct object - no preposition needed.
Imperative tu form of -are verbs ends in -a.
Imperative tu form of 'andare' is 'vai'.

english: Yesterday I went to the cinema.
explanation: 'Andare' takes 'essere' as auxiliary; participle agrees with subject.
'Mangiare' takes 'avere'; participle stays invariable with avere.
'Visto' is the irregular past participle of vedere.
Reflexive verbs always take essere; participle agrees with subject.

english: She got up early this morning.
explanation: 'Alzata' (feminine singular) because subject is 'lei'.
'Fatto' is the irregular past participle of fare.
'Nel' = in + il, used before years.

english: I have lived here for two years.
explanation: Italian uses present tense with 'da' for actions still ongoing.
Modal verbs (dovere/potere/volere) take an infinitive directly.
'Potere' for permission/ability; followed by infinitive.
Definite article often precedes language names.
'Sapere + infinitive' = to know how to (skill).
'Conoscere' for people/places; 'sapere' for facts/skills.

english: I'd like a glass of red wine.
italian: Vorrei un bicchiere di vino rosso.
explanation: 'Vorrei' (conditional of volere) is more polite than 'voglio'.

english: Could you tell me the time?
explanation: 'Potresti' (conditional) for polite requests; 'dirmi' = dire + mi.

english: I'm reading a book about Italy.
explanation: 'Sull'' = su + l' (about/on).

english: He is sleeping in his room.
explanation: Possessive 'sua' agrees with 'camera' (feminine).
'Pensare a' = to think about; 'pensare di' for opinions.

english: Tomorrow I will leave for Rome.
explanation: 'Partirò' = io form of futuro; 'per' = for/toward.

english: We will see each other tomorrow.
explanation: Reciprocal action: 'ci' (each other) + vedremo (we will see).
Object pronoun 'ti' goes before the conjugated verb.
'Forse' = maybe; 'pioverà' = it will rain (no subject pronoun).

english: I would like to travel more.
explanation: 'Di più' = more (as quantity).

english: If I have time, I'll come.
explanation: Periodo ipotetico tipo 1: present in both clauses for likely conditions.
'Pensare che' typically triggers the subjunctive ('abbia' from avere).

english: I don't know if he'll come.
explanation: 'Se' = whether/if; followed by indicative for indirect questions.
Adverbs of manner often end in '-mente' (like English '-ly').
Negative tu imperative = non + infinitive.
Object pronoun attaches to affirmative imperative: ascolta + mi.
'Dammelo' = da + mi + lo (give + me + it). Mi → me before lo/la.

english: I had already left when she arrived.
italian: Ero già partito quando è arrivata.
explanation: Trapassato prossimo (had + verb) for an action before another past action.

english: If I were rich, I would travel.
explanation: Periodo ipotetico tipo 2: imperfect subjunctive + present conditional.

english: I want you to come tonight.
explanation: 'Volere che' triggers the subjunctive: 'venga' (present subjunctive of venire).

english: It's necessary that we leave early.
explanation: Impersonal 'è necessario che' triggers subjunctive 'partiamo'.

english: The book that I'm reading is interesting.
italian: Il libro che sto leggendo è interessante.
explanation: 'Che' (relative) = that/which; can refer to subject or object.

english: The friend with whom I went to Rome.
italian: L'amico con cui sono andato a Roma.
explanation: After prepositions, use 'cui' (not che) as the relative pronoun.

english: I have known her for many years.
explanation: Italian uses simple present (not present perfect) with 'da' for ongoing situations.

english: Although it's raining, we'll go out.
explanation: 'Sebbene' (although) triggers subjunctive: 'piova' (subj. of piovere).

english: Before going out, I closed the windows.
italian: Prima di uscire, ho chiuso le finestre.
explanation: 'Prima di + infinitive' = before + verb-ing.

english: After eating, I went for a walk.
italian: Dopo aver mangiato, ho fatto una passeggiata.
explanation: 'Dopo + infinito passato' (aver + past participle) = after + verb-ing.

english: I had to leave early because I was tired.
italian: Ho dovuto andare via presto perché ero stanco.
explanation: Mixed past tenses: passato prossimo for one-time, imperfetto for state.

english: She told me that she was happy.
italian: Mi ha detto che era felice.
explanation: In indirect speech, present tense becomes imperfetto (era).

english: I wonder where she has gone.
explanation: Doubt or wonder + indirect question often takes subjunctive.

english: It seems that he doesn't want to come.
explanation: Impersonal 'sembra che' triggers subjunctive 'voglia'.

english: The harder I try, the worse it goes.
explanation: Italian construction: più...più (the more...the more); più...meno (the more...the less).
'Come' = as; no article before profession with 'lavorare come'.

english: I would have liked to come.
explanation: Condizionale passato of modal: essere/avere conditional + past participle + infinitive.

english: If I had known, I would have come.
explanation: Periodo ipotetico tipo 3: trapassato congiuntivo + condizionale passato.
'Fare + infinitive' = to make/have someone do something.

italian: Mi sono fatto tagliare i capelli.
explanation: 'Farsi + infinitive' = to have something done to oneself.
'Vale la pena' = it's worth + verb-ing; pronoun attaches to infinitive.

english: I'm used to getting up early.
explanation: 'Ad' (instead of 'a') before vowels for euphony.

english: He stopped smoking three years ago.
italian: Ha smesso di fumare tre anni fa.
explanation: 'Fa' (ago) goes after the time expression: tre anni fa = three years ago.

italian: Non sono mai stato a Napoli.
explanation: 'Non...mai' = never; 'mai' goes between auxiliary and participle.
'Chiunque' (whoever) triggers the subjunctive.

grammar_point: object pronoun in past + per + stress pronoun
explanation: 'L''=lo (it); 'comprato' agrees with 'lo' (m.sg).
In Italian, 'would come' (after past) uses condizionale passato, not present conditional.

italian: Nonostante la difficoltà, ci sono riuscito.
explanation: 'Nonostante' + noun (or + congiuntivo before clause).

english: I doubt he is telling the truth.
explanation: 'Dubitare che' (to doubt that) takes subjunctive.

english: I want to talk about it.
explanation: 'Ne' (about it/of it) attaches to the infinitive.
'Ci' replaces a place: there. Goes before auxiliary.
Specific construction for stating a group's size.

english: It's been a long time since I saw you.
italian: È molto tempo che non ti vedo.
explanation: 'È...che' construction; uses present tense of the ongoing action.
